questions.title: Missing Owners
questions.story_md: Both queries run. **Find staff with no box. `boxes.owner_id` can be NULL.** Choose one and say why.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE staff (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, bonus INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE boxes (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner_id INTEGER, size TEXT);

options.text_md: NOT IN cannot use a subquery
If the subquery returns a NULL, NOT IN is never true, so A returns nothing

questions.title: Zero Means Zero
questions.story_md: Both queries run. **Every account must show its transaction count, 0 when it has none.** Choose one and say why.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, branch TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT);
CREATE TABLE transactions (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, amount INTEGER, at TEXT);

options.text_md: B is faster because it reads fewer columns
COUNT(*) is not allowed with GROUP BY
COUNT(t.id) skips the NULL row the LEFT JOIN adds; COUNT(*) counts it as 1

questions.title: Row and Total
questions.story_md: Both queries run. **Each transaction must be listed with its account's total next to it.** Choose one and say why.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, branch TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT);
CREATE TABLE transactions (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, amount INTEGER, at TEXT);

options.text_md: GROUP BY cannot SUM negative amounts
A window keeps every row and adds the group total; GROUP BY collapses rows to one per account
Windows are always faster than GROUP BY

questions.title: Every Movement
questions.story_md: Both queries run. **Every deposit and every withdrawal must be listed, even two that look identical.** Choose one and say why.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, branch TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT);
CREATE TABLE transactions (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, amount INTEGER, at TEXT);

options.text_md: UNION cannot combine one table with itself
UNION removes identical rows (and sorts to find them); UNION ALL keeps them all
A returns more rows than B

questions.title: Exactly One Each
questions.story_md: Both queries run. **Exactly one top earner per department is needed, even when two earn the same.** Choose one and say why.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, manager_id INTEGER);

options.text_md: ROW_NUMBER is the only function allowed in a subquery
RANK gives tied rows the same number, so A can return two people per department
A is wrong because it has no tie-break, so it errors

questions.title: A Huge Table
questions.story_md: Both queries run. **The transactions table has 50 million rows and an index on `at`. You need March 2025.** Choose one and say why.

options.text_md: A cannot run on large tables
B compares the column itself, so the index on at can jump to March; A must compute strftime for every row

questions.title: Said Twice
questions.story_md: Both queries run. **The same "big accounts" subquery is needed twice, and a teammate must be able to check it.** Choose one and say why.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, branch TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT);
CREATE TABLE transactions (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, amount INTEGER, at TEXT);

options.text_md: The CTE defines the rule once, so it cannot drift between the two copies and is easier to read
CTEs are the only way to use AVG

questions.title: Deposits Only
questions.story_md: Both queries run. **Sum only the deposits (amount > 0) of each account.** Choose one and say why.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, branch TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT);
CREATE TABLE transactions (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, amount INTEGER, at TEXT);

options.text_md: HAVING is slower but gives the same answer
WHERE drops withdrawals before summing; HAVING only drops whole accounts after summing everything
WHERE cannot be used with GROUP BY

questions.title: Who Moved Big Money
questions.story_md: Both queries run. **List each owner with at least one transaction over 2000, once, on a large table.** Choose one and say why.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, branch TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT);
CREATE TABLE transactions (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, amount INTEGER, at TEXT);

options.text_md: A misses owners with one transaction
DISTINCT is not allowed with JOIN
EXISTS stops at the first match and never makes duplicates; the join makes them and DISTINCT removes them again

questions.title: Totals Without an Index
questions.story_md: Both queries run. **There is no index on `transactions.account_id`, and both tables are large.** Choose one and say why.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, branch TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT);
CREATE TABLE transactions (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, amount INTEGER, at TEXT);

options.text_md: Without the index A reads all transactions once per account; B can do the work in one grouped pass
Subqueries are not allowed in SELECT

questions.title: The Five Newest
questions.story_md: Both queries run. **Show the five newest transactions.** Choose one and say why.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, branch TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT);
CREATE TABLE transactions (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, amount INTEGER, at TEXT);

options.text_md: Without ORDER BY the database may return any five rows; LIMIT alone does not mean newest
LIMIT needs ORDER BY or it errors

questions.title: Fair Average
questions.story_md: Both queries run. **The average balance must keep its decimals.** Choose one and say why.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, branch TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT);
CREATE TABLE transactions (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, amount INTEGER, at TEXT);

options.text_md: SUM / COUNT of integers is integer division in SQLite, which drops the decimals

questions.title: Nothing Is Zero
questions.story_md: Both queries run. **Accounts without transactions must show a total of 0, not empty.** Choose one and say why.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, branch TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT);
CREATE TABLE transactions (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, amount INTEGER, at TEXT);

options.text_md: SUM over no rows is NULL; COALESCE turns it into 0

questions.title: How Deep Is the Chain
questions.story_md: Both queries run. **Find everyone under employee 1, however many levels down the chain goes.** Choose one and say why.
questions.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary INTEGER, manager_id INTEGER);

options.text_md: The self-joins stop at a fixed depth (two levels); the recursive CTE follows the chain until it ends
The CTE is faster on every table

questions.title: Storing Money
questions.story_md: Both queries run. **Balances must add up to the exact cent across millions of rows.** Choose one and say why.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT, branch TEXT, balance INTEGER, opened TEXT);
CREATE TABLE transactions (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER, amount INTEGER, at TEXT);

options.text_md: INTEGER columns take less space, which is the only reason
REAL is binary floating point: 0.1 cannot be stored exactly, so sums drift; whole cents add up exactly
